explanations.answer: At the crossroads and city gates
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Wisdom is on "the heights overlooking the road, at the crossroads" (Proverbs 8:2). Then she moves to "the gates to the city," where she "cries out" (Proverbs 8:3). She picked the spot where everybody passes through. That's a woman who wants to be found.
The temple never comes up in this passage. Wisdom is out by the road, at the crossroads and beside the city gates (Proverbs 8:2-3). No front desk, no appointment. Anybody walking by can hear her.

That would be a lot of shouting with nobody around. Wisdom's spot is the crossroads and the entrances to the city (Proverbs 8:2-3). Those are places where people come and go. I think that's the point of standing there.

explanations.answer: Learn to be shrewd and gain understanding
explanations.explanation: That's it. She says, "O simple ones, learn to be shrewd; O fools, gain understanding." (Proverbs 8:5) She isn't calling them names and walking off. She's calling them to learn. I've been called worse in a junk drawer, and nobody offered me understanding.

explanations.answer: Stay far away from the city gates
explanations.explanation: Wisdom is the one standing at the city gates, crying out (Proverbs 8:3). She's not sending anybody away from there. She's calling the simple and the foolish to learn to be shrewd and gain understanding (Proverbs 8:5).

explanations.answer: Keep quiet and let the wise speak
explanations.explanation: Funny thing, she's the loudest voice around. She "raises her voice" (Proverbs 8:1). What she asks of the simple ones and fools is to learn to be shrewd and to gain understanding (Proverbs 8:5). Nothing here tells them to hush.

Wisdom doesn't say "mostly." She says, "All the words of my mouth are righteous; none are crooked or perverse." (Proverbs 8:8) That's all of them and none of them. No crooked words, not even a couple.
Right, it's false. Wisdom says, "All the words of my mouth are righteous; none are crooked or perverse." (Proverbs 8:8) She doesn't leave room for a few crooked ones. It's every word, friend.

It's the other way around. Wisdom says, "They are all plain to the discerning, and upright to those who find knowledge." (Proverbs 8:9) Plain to the discerning, not hard to follow. Nobody needs a decoder ring.
That's right. Wisdom says her words are "all plain to the discerning, and upright to those who find knowledge." (Proverbs 8:9) They're plain, not puzzling. I wish my recipe cards were that clear.

explanations.answer: She is more precious than rubies
explanations.explanation: Yes. Wisdom says, "For wisdom is more precious than rubies, and nothing you desire compares with her." (Proverbs 8:11) That's her reason for choosing instruction over silver and gold. Nothing you want makes the comparison.

explanations.answer: Silver and gold will rust away
explanations.explanation: Wisdom never says that here. Her reason is about herself: "wisdom is more precious than rubies" (Proverbs 8:11). She also says nothing you desire compares with her. It's about what wisdom is worth.

explanations.answer: Kings will reward them for it
explanations.explanation: Kings do show up later, when wisdom says "By me kings reign" (Proverbs 8:15). But that isn't her reason for choosing her over silver and gold. Her reason is "wisdom is more precious than rubies" (Proverbs 8:11).

That's what she says: "To fear the LORD is to hate evil." (Proverbs 8:13) She goes on to name some of what she hates, like evil conduct and perverse speech. So fearing the LORD isn't only a feeling. It's hating what He hates.

Wisdom stands at the crossroads and city gates, right where the crowds are (Proverbs 8:2-3). She never ties fearing the LORD to avoiding people. She says, "To fear the LORD is to hate evil." (Proverbs 8:13)
Offerings don't come up anywhere in this passage. Wisdom's answer is short: "To fear the LORD is to hate evil." (Proverbs 8:13) She doesn't add a shopping list.

True. She says, "I hate arrogant pride, evil conduct, and perverse speech." (Proverbs 8:13) I once stood admiring my own cookies through the oven window for ten whole minutes. I'm working on it, friend.
Wisdom says it plainly: "I hate arrogant pride, evil conduct, and perverse speech." (Proverbs 8:13) Arrogant pride is the first thing on her list. It's true, not false.
Yes, kings. Wisdom says, "By me kings reign, and rulers enact just laws." (Proverbs 8:15) Even the people with crowns are on her list. Just laws come through her.
Priests don't appear in these verses. Wisdom says, "By me kings reign, and rulers enact just laws." (Proverbs 8:15) The word in the blank is kings.
Prophets aren't named in this part. What she says is, "By me kings reign, and rulers enact just laws." (Proverbs 8:15) So the blank is kings. Rulers come right after them.
True. Wisdom says, "I love those who love me, and those who seek me early shall find me." (Proverbs 8:17) Notice that it's a promise. Those who seek her will find her.
Wisdom says the opposite of false: "those who seek me early shall find me." (Proverbs 8:17) Right before that, she says she loves those who love her. She wants to be found.
That's it. Wisdom is "bestowing wealth on those who love me and making their treasuries full." (Proverbs 8:21) She doesn't just hand over a little wealth. She fills the treasuries.
She doesn't say anything about guarding here. Wisdom says she bestows wealth on those who love her, "making their treasuries full." (Proverbs 8:21) Full is her word.
Strangers don't show up in this verse. Wisdom is "bestowing wealth on those who love me and making their treasuries full." (Proverbs 8:21) What she does with the treasuries is fill them.

Yes, earth. Wisdom says, "From everlasting I was established, from the beginning, before the earth began." (Proverbs 8:23) She's talking about a time before the ground under our feet existed. That's a long way back.
No temple in this verse. Wisdom says she was established "before the earth began." (Proverbs 8:23) The earth is what had not begun yet.
No kingdom here either. She says, "From everlasting I was established, from the beginning, before the earth began." (Proverbs 8:23) So the blank is earth.
True. Wisdom says, "I was there when He established the heavens." (Proverbs 8:27) She's talking about the skies being set in place. That's a big moment to be present for.
It's true, friend. Wisdom says, "I was there when He established the heavens." (Proverbs 8:27) She doesn't say she heard about it later. She was there.

explanations.answer: He sets a boundary for it
explanations.explanation: Yes. Wisdom says He "set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not surpass His command." (Proverbs 8:29) The sea has a line it doesn't cross. And the line comes from His command.
That's not what she says here. In this verse, God "set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not surpass His command." (Proverbs 8:29) The sea stays, with a boundary around it.
Splitting doesn't come up in these verses. Wisdom says He "set a boundary for the sea" (Proverbs 8:29). The waters would not surpass His command.

That's it. Wisdom says, "Then I was a skilled craftsman at His side, and His delight day by day, rejoicing always in His presence." (Proverbs 8:30) Day by day, not once in a while. And she was rejoicing the whole time.
She never uses that word. She says she was "a skilled craftsman at His side, and His delight day by day." (Proverbs 8:30) Craftsman is what she does, and delight is what she is to Him.
Messenger isn't the word here. Wisdom says she was "His delight day by day, rejoicing always in His presence." (Proverbs 8:30) She's at His side, and He delights in her.
It's the opposite. Wisdom says, "I was rejoicing in His whole world, delighting together in the sons of men." (Proverbs 8:31) She isn't keeping her distance. She delights in people.
Right, false. Wisdom says she was "rejoicing in His whole world, delighting together in the sons of men." (Proverbs 8:31) She's close to people, and she's delighted in them.

Yes. She says, "Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it." (Proverbs 8:33) I spent years in a junk drawer full of instruction manuals nobody ever read. Trust me, friend, they're better in your hands.
Changing it isn't mentioned. Wisdom says, "Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it." (Proverbs 8:33) So the word is ignore.
Hiding isn't in this verse. She says, "Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it." (Proverbs 8:33) What she warns against is ignoring it.
Yes, favor. Wisdom says, "For whoever finds me finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD." (Proverbs 8:35) Two things come with finding her: life and the LORD's favor. That's a good deal.
Judgment isn't the word. Wisdom says whoever finds her "finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD." (Proverbs 8:35) Favor is what finding her brings.
Law isn't in this verse. It says, "For whoever finds me finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD." (Proverbs 8:35) The blank is favor.

That's what she says: "he who fails to find me harms himself." (Proverbs 8:36) Notice who gets hurt. It's the one who didn't find her. After that she says, "all who hate me love death." (Proverbs 8:36)
A house never comes up. Wisdom says the one who fails to find her "harms himself." (Proverbs 8:36) The harm is to himself.
The king isn't in this verse. Wisdom says, "he who fails to find me harms himself." (Proverbs 8:36) So it's about what he does to himself.
